correctness.rationale: For \(F=u f^{\mathsf T}\), the nonnegative rank-one matrix \(FV^{-1}\) has spectral radius \(f^{\mathsf T}V^{-1}u\). Sherman--Morrison applied to \(V+tuw^{\mathsf T}\) has denominator \(1+t w^{\mathsf T}V^{-1}u>0\), gives the displayed inverse exactly, and yields \(V_t^{-1}u=V^{-1}u/(1+ts)\). Under the explicitly stated inverse-positivity condition, \(F_tV_t^{-1}\) is nonnegative rank one, so its spectral radius is exactly \((R_0+ts)/(1+ts)\). The concrete source formulas reduce to the common numerator \(AD-B(C+D)\), proving their stated contraction factor. No numerical inference is used.

originality.rationale: The closest recent source explicitly foregrounds non-uniqueness of regular splittings and, separately, a common-target heuristic for keeping the next-generation matrix low rank, but it does not state an exact transformation law for the reproduction number. The older non-uniqueness paper gives several competing formulas and threshold equivalences, and classical regular-splitting comparison theorems give qualitative spectral-radius ordering. None of the inspected sources or semantic database results supplies the exact aligned-transfer inverse-positivity criterion together with \(R_t-1=(R_0-1)/(1+ts)\), nor the strict source-specific contraction between equations (16) and (17).
residual_risks: The exact identity may exist in older numerical-linear-algebra literature as an unstated or differently named special case of rank-one updates to regular splittings.

The matrix theorem is elementary once the aligned update is recognized; originality rests on the exact structural formulation and its connection to nonunique reproduction numbers, not on novelty of the Sherman--Morrison identity itself.
Negative semantic/database searches do not constitute a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The result addresses a mathematically explicit gap created by nonunique next-generation splittings: threshold equivalence alone does not say how far two valid reproduction numbers can differ. The theorem gives an exact deformation law and an exact admissibility test for the rank-one/common-row regime singled out by recent low-rank splitting algorithms. The source-specific corollary turns two published competing formulas into a strict quantitative ordering around the bifurcation threshold. This is a reusable structural lemma rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a numerical recomputation.
